literal: While we see with our eyes, those who lack understanding laugh, because they themselves have not suffered what we have suffered.
translation: Those who lack understanding laugh at me right before my eyes, only because they themselves have never suffered the pain that I have suffered.
modern: நாங்கள் எங்கள் கண்களால் பார்க்கும்படி, அறிவு இல்லாதவர்கள் எங்களைப் பார்த்துச் சிரிக்கிறார்கள்; நாங்கள் அனுபவித்த துன்பங்களை அவர்கள் அனுபவிக்காத காரணத்தால் தான்.
explanation: In this couplet, the lover laments the mockery of the townspeople who do not comprehend the agony of love-sickness. The phrase 'arivillār' refers to these onlookers, whom the lover calls 'lacking in understanding' because they lack empathy. They laugh openly right in front of the lover's eyes ('kaṇṇiṉ kāṇa nakupa'). The lover explains that this ridicule happens only because these people have never themselves experienced ('tām paṭā') the intense suffering ('yām paṭṭa') that the lover is going through.
